Galbraith’s ideas reached government through the Democratic Party, first as a speechwriter and adviser to Adlai Stevenson in the 1950s and then in John F. Kennedy’s 1960 campaign.
Kennedy named him ambassador to India, a post he held from 1961 to 1963. It included the weeks of the 1962 border war between India and China, when he helped arrange American support for New Delhi. He kept a diary that became Ambassador’s Journal (1969). At home, his preference was for public spending over tax cuts. Kennedy’s Council of Economic Advisers pushed the tax cut, and it was enacted in 1964, a year after Galbraith had returned to Harvard.
